blocks.text: **The problem.** Given an `m × n` grid of letters `board` and a string `word`, return `true` if the word can be spelled by a path of **adjacent** cells (up, down, left or right). The same cell may not be used twice in one word.

blocks.alt: The board A B C E / S F C S / A D E E and the word ABCCED. The path starts at the top-left A, goes right to B and C, down to the C below, down to E, and left to D. Each step moves to a neighbour that holds the next letter, and no cell is used twice.

blocks.text: The last chapter backtracks over **positions on a grid or board** instead of items in a list: the next letter of a word in a neighbouring cell, a queen in the next row, a digit in the next empty square. The template is the same — choose, explore, un-choose — and the board itself records the choices (mark a cell, place a queen, write a digit) so un-choosing means **restoring the board**. Strong pruning is what makes these hard problems run fast.
The idea: DFS from every cell, marking the path

Try every cell as the start. From a cell holding `word[i]`, look for `word[i + 1]` in its four neighbours. To stop a path from reusing a cell, **mark it** (overwrite it with `#`) while it's on the path, and **restore** it when backing out — that's the un-choose step. The search stops as soon as the whole word is matched.

blocks.caption: The path grows into neighbours holding the next letter; cells on the path are marked so they can't be reused.

blocks.text: **Time O(m · n · 3ᴸ)** for a word of length L: every start cell, then at most 3 new directions per step (the fourth is where you came from). **Space O(L)** for the call stack; marking in place needs no visited array.

Two cheap checks often decide the answer — or shrink the search — before any DFS: if the board doesn't contain enough of some letter, return false at once; and if the word's last letter is rarer on the board than its first, search for the **reversed** word, so far fewer starting cells match.
**Same worst case**, but these two checks turn the classic slow test cases — a board full of A's and a word of A's ending in B — from seconds into microseconds.

blocks.alt: DFS + marking: O(m·n·3^L) time, O(L) space. Count first, rarer end: O(m·n·3^L) time, O(L) space.

items: **Reusing a cell** — `"ABCB"` must fail; forgetting to mark lets the path step back onto B.
**Word longer than the board** — false straight away.
**Restore the board** — the next starting cell must see the original letters.
**Word Search II** — many words at once: walk the board with a **trie** so one DFS checks every word.
**Number of Islands** — DFS over a grid marking cells, without un-marking (Graph course).
**Unique Paths III** — visit every empty square exactly once: the same mark / un-mark backtracking.
